criteria.text: Clinical evidence of mycosis of the nail by generally accepted clinical findings
criteria.source_span: Clinical evidence of mycosis of the nail, by generally accepted clinical findings such as discoloration, onycholysis, subungual debris, thickening, or secondary skin infection

criteria.text: One of the ambulatory/non-ambulatory documentation criteria must be met for mycotic toenails
sub_conditions: the ambulatory patient has marked limitation of ambulation, pain, or secondary infection resulting from the thickening and dystrophy of the infected toenail plate(s)
the non-ambulatory patient suffers from pain or secondary infection resulting from the thickening and dystrophy of the infected toenail plate(s)
criteria.source_span: In addition one of the following must be documented for mycotic toenails:

criteria.text: Appropriate anti-fungal treatment is necessary to qualify nail debridement as medically necessary, unless contraindicated (and the contraindication must be documented if not used)
criteria.source_span: Appropriate anti-fungal treatment is necessary to qualify nail debridement as a medically necessary and reimbursable service unless contraindicated. If an anti-fungal treatment is not used, the contraindication must be documented in the medical record.

criteria.text: Patients need not have an underlying systemic condition to be covered for mycotic nail care
criteria.source_span: Patients need not have an underlying systemic condition to be covered for mycotic nail care.
